editorial.title: Node.js security updates address HTTP/2 crashes and memory disclosure
editorial.summary: The Node.js November 11 security release fixes HTTP/2 denial-of-service and memory-disclosure issues, an HTTPS parser re-entrancy flaw, and other bugs. The project provides 22.23.5, 24.22.3 and 26.13.1; affected release lines and trigger conditions vary by issue.
editorial.why_it_matters: Applications serving HTTP/2 or handling the affected HTTPS patterns need runtime updates. Updating application dependencies alone does not replace the Node.js runtime.
editorial.action: Move to the security release for your supported Node.js line, rebuild deployed images and check running versions. Consult the upstream per-issue scope before claiming a deployment is unaffected.
